messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — RFC merged for migrating the public text-generation contract. /v1/generate -> /v2/generate. v2 changes: streaming chunk format, partial token metadata, and a small body shape tweak (outputs -> choices). Need to decide shim/compat strategy + deprecation timeline.

maya: thanks. do we have an SDK plan? most customers call via SDKs not raw curl. we should avoid breaking them.

alex: agree. options: 1) runtime gateway shim that accepts v1 and rewrites to v2, 2) SDKs include client-side adapter, 3) dual support on server for a limited time. tradeoffs: latency, maintenance, and tech debt.

sam: gateway shim seems lowest friction for customers but higher cost/complexity for infra. rewriting streaming format is hairy — we'd need to buffer to convert shapes unless we stream transform. that adds CPU.

maya: can we do header-based opt-in? e.g., `X-Redwood-API-Version: 1` to force old behaviour, default to v2. Then have gateway translate only when header present. minimizes heat.

julie: add telemetry needs: track how many requests use the header, error delta pre/post, token cost changes. also need to surface to console per-customer so account teams can reach out.

alex: good call. proposed rollout: short term shim that handles basic shape change (outputs -> choices) and status mapping; streaming polyfill later. timeline: shim for shape within 2 weeks, SDK adapters published in 3 weeks, streaming conversion as experimental toggle in 6 weeks, then 6 months deprecation window. thoughts?

sam: can we do canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across backends? infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary pipeline available — use tag `compat-v1-shim` with rollout steps in deploy config.

maya: also need tests: e2e with customer sample prompts (long streaming, short non-streaming, function-calls). Add golden prompt set for regression alerts.

julie: legal/comms: draft notice to customers at 90/60/30/14/7 days before forced switch. include migration guide and snippet for SDKs.

sam: operational concerns: mapping error codes — v2 returns 422 for validation instead of 400 sometimes. shim should normalize to previous 400 to avoid breaking clients. also map new retry-after headers to our existing backoff logic.

alex: good. for performance, implement lightweight path first: header-based simple JSON remap for non-streaming. streaming: provide `stream_transform=polyfill` query flag to let callers opt-in; gradual automatic conversion later.

maya: SDK work: add `compatMode: 'v1' | 'v2'` option, default autodetect from server header, and surface deprecation warning at runtime. we'll coordinate releases with shim rollout.

julie: ops: how do we measure success? propose metrics: percent of requests hitting shim, error rate delta per-customer, avg latency delta, and token cost delta. set alert thresholds (error rate > 0.5% relative increase).

sam: add load tests for shim under real traffic shapes — client-side batching bursts, long tokens, many small requests. aim to keep p95 added latency < 12ms.

alex: next steps: 1) sam to prototype slim gateway remap + perf bench (due in 3 business days). 2) maya to start SDK adapter PR (branch: compat/client-adapter). 3) julie to draft customer comms and telemetry dashboard. 4) infra-bot to create canary job. I'll publish rollout plan doc and link in #eng-docs.

infra-bot: created canary job `compat-v1-shim` — https://ci.redwood/jobs/compat-v1-shim

maya: ack. I'll add sample code for migration: ```js
// SDK example
const client = new Redwood({ compatMode: 'v1' });
const r = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hello' });
```

alex: thanks all. keep notes here with any blocking issues. if someone has a heavy customer on v1, ping me and we'll prioritize Per-customer long-lived shim. :thumbsup:
